title: The Wallace Index — internally reviewed qualitative drafts
scope: Five full-period research scopes; selected start/middle/end cases reviewed. Not an exhaustive full-period assessment.

sources.title: The Rt Hon Boris Johnson
sources.factual_summary: The biography gives the premiership as 24 July 2019 to 6 September 2022.
sources.reliability_and_relevance_notes: Chronology only. Dynamic page; original publication date is not supplied.
sources.locator: Biography

sources.title: R (Miller) v The Prime Minister; Cherry v Advocate General for Scotland
sources.factual_summary: The Court held the advice to prorogue Parliament unlawful and the resulting prorogation null and without effect.
sources.reliability_and_relevance_notes: A legal finding about the exercise of a power. Do not turn it into a finding of criminality or a general character judgement. Examine the recorded government arguments and subsequent compliance.
sources.archival_reference: [2019] UKSC 41; National Archives Find Case Law
sources.locator: [2019] UKSC 41, paragraphs 50, 61 and 69–70

sources.title: Matter referred on 21 April 2022 (conduct of Rt Hon Boris Johnson): Final Report — Summary
sources.author_or_issuing_institution: House of Commons Committee of Privileges
sources.factual_summary: The Committee concluded that Johnson deliberately misled the House. The summary records its reasoning, his denials and his response to provisional conclusions.
sources.reliability_and_relevance_notes: Later finding partly concerns statements during the premiership, but also later conduct. Exclude post-premiership conduct from the scored period. Read the full evidence, Johnson’s representations and the Commons decision before assessment.
sources.locator: Summary, paragraphs 11–17

sources.title: Coronavirus: lessons learned to date report published
sources.author_or_issuing_institution: Commons Science and Technology Committee and Health and Social Care Committee
sources.factual_summary: The committees identified both vaccination successes and serious weaknesses in the early pandemic response, including delayed lockdown and shortcomings affecting vulnerable groups.
sources.reliability_and_relevance_notes: An official summary of a collective institutional response, not a personal verdict on Johnson. The underlying report, decision records and subsequent inquiry findings still require review.
sources.locator: Opening summary and principal findings

sources.title: Prime Minister pledges UK’s unwavering support to Ukraine on visit to Kyiv: 9 April 2022
sources.factual_summary: The government recorded Johnson’s Kyiv visit and announced additional military assistance and World Bank lending guarantees.
sources.reliability_and_relevance_notes: Primary evidence of the announcement and stated policy. Verify delivery and the leader’s decision-making independently; the release does not establish motives or effectiveness.
sources.locator: Paragraphs describing assistance and lending guarantees

sources.title: The Rt Hon Sir Keir Starmer KCB KC MP
sources.factual_summary: The retrieved biography states that Starmer was Prime Minister from 5 July 2024 to 20 July 2026.
sources.reliability_and_relevance_notes: Dynamic page. Treat these as source-reported boundaries pending a second dated institutional check; do not silently carry forward an open-ended period.
sources.locator: Biography

sources.title: New Ministerial Code to set out standards in public life and restore transparency
sources.author_or_issuing_institution: Cabinet Office and Independent Adviser on Ministerial Standards
sources.factual_summary: The announcement sets out monthly publication of ministerial gifts and hospitality, including values, and an independent adviser’s power to initiate investigations without a prime ministerial veto.
sources.reliability_and_relevance_notes: Announced institutional rules are not evidence of consistent compliance or enforcement. Check the fixed November 2024 code and subsequent disclosures rather than a later amended code.
sources.locator: Gifts and hospitality rules; independent adviser powers

sources.title: Register of Members’ Financial Interests: Starmer, Sir Keir (14 October 2024)
sources.factual_summary: The register includes Arsenal tickets and hospitality received on 17 August 2024 and declared on 10 September 2024. Other entries concern earlier dates or periods straddling the start of the premiership.
sources.reliability_and_relevance_notes: Disclosure establishes the declared benefit, not improper influence or a breach. Filter by receipt/acceptance dates, not registration date. Seek applicable rules, corrections, findings and the leader’s response.
sources.locator: Category 3; Arsenal entry received 17 August 2024; accommodation entry 29 May–13 July 2024

sources.title: Plan for Change
sources.factual_summary: The publication record identifies the Plan for Change and states it was presented to Parliament on 5 December 2024.
sources.reliability_and_relevance_notes: Only the publication landing page was reviewed. The 48-page attachment, resources, milestones, implementation and later revisions have not been examined.
sources.locator: Details and document metadata: CP 1210, ISBN 978-1-5286-5291-9

sources.title: PM statement: 4 August 2024
sources.factual_summary: Starmer condemned violent disorder, referred to targeted Muslim and other minority communities, and stated that the government would support the police and pursue criminal enforcement.
sources.reliability_and_relevance_notes: Evidence of words delivered. Assess tone, uncertainty, proportionality, implementation and community experience separately; forceful language is not by itself a crisis score.
sources.locator: Speech transcript, paragraphs on targeted communities and policing

sources.title: Nine million pensioners to receive Winter Fuel Payments this winter
sources.factual_summary: The Treasury announced expanded Winter Fuel Payment eligibility in England and Wales using a £35,000 income threshold, following the narrower arrangements introduced for winter 2024/25.
sources.reliability_and_relevance_notes: A Treasury announcement, not proof of Starmer’s personal reasoning. Recover the original regulations, consultation, impact analysis and decision record. Revision may reflect responsiveness, inconsistency or both; do not infer motives.
sources.locator: Eligibility announcement and Further background

sources.title: Greater Manchester to vote for new Mayor
sources.factual_summary: Discovery lead for the end of Burnham’s mayoralty. No claim is admitted from this inaccessible page.
sources.reliability_and_relevance_notes: Search results report a vacancy on 19 June 2026, but direct retrieval failed with HTTP 402. Confirm through dated election or council records before fixing the period.
sources.locator: Election vacancy notice

sources.title: The Kerslake Report
sources.author_or_issuing_institution: Lord Kerslake and independent review panel
sources.factual_summary: Discovery lead for the independent review of preparedness and response to the Manchester Arena attack.
sources.reliability_and_relevance_notes: Direct retrieval failed. Do not attribute any specific report finding or personal credit to Burnham from this lead. Recover the report, commissioning record and implementation follow-up.
sources.locator: Full report; family evidence and recommendations

sources.title: An inspection of the service provided to victims of crime by Greater Manchester Police
sources.author_or_issuing_institution: HM Inspectorate of Constabulary and Fire & Rescue Services
sources.factual_summary: The inspection identified serious weaknesses in victim service, crime recording, investigation and governance, while recognising some improvements and a programme of change.
sources.reliability_and_relevance_notes: The reviewed passages concern the police force. Determine the mayor’s oversight powers, knowledge, delegation and response before individual attribution. Exact publication date remains unverified.
sources.locator: Printed pages 8–12: summary, supervision and governance, causes of concern; inspection conducted September–October 2020

sources.title: Greater Manchester Police Most Improved Force in the Country as Chief Constable and Mayor confirm HMICFRS has removed Force from Special Measures
sources.factual_summary: The police force announced removal from enhanced monitoring and described improvements in call handling, recording and investigation.
sources.reliability_and_relevance_notes: This is the force’s own account of improvement, not the inspectorate’s original determination. Retrieve that determination and mayoral scrutiny records. Do not treat increased arrests as proof of moral leadership.
sources.locator: Opening announcement and crime-recording/investigation passages

sources.title: Bus Franchising
sources.factual_summary: Discovery lead for the franchising decision, consultation and delivery record.
sources.reliability_and_relevance_notes: Direct retrieval failed with HTTP 402. Recover the original 2021 decision, consultation findings, legal record, financial assessments and subsequent performance evidence.
sources.locator: Bus franchising overview

sources.title: President Barack Obama
sources.author_or_issuing_institution: Barack Obama Presidential Library, National Archives and Records Administration
sources.factual_summary: The archival biography records Obama’s inauguration on 20 January 2009 and return to private life on 20 January 2017.
sources.reliability_and_relevance_notes: Chronology and initial pointers only. This institutional biography is not an independent assessment of leadership.
sources.locator: Political Career and Post-Presidency

sources.title: Healthcare.gov: Ineffective Planning and Oversight Practices Underscore the Need for Improved Contract Management
sources.factual_summary: GAO identified inadequate CMS planning and oversight, increased contract costs and delayed functionality. The record includes agency responses and later implementation of recommendations.
sources.reliability_and_relevance_notes: The audit concerns CMS and contracts, not a finding of presidential personal misconduct. Separate the original audit from later updates and trace White House oversight and corrective decisions.
sources.locator: What GAO Found; Recommendations for Executive Action

sources.title: Report on the Telephone Records Program Conducted under Section 215 and on the Operations of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Court
sources.author_or_issuing_institution: Privacy and Civil Liberties Oversight Board
sources.publisher: PCLOB; copy hosted by US Senate Judiciary Committee
sources.factual_summary: The Board recommended ending bulk telephone-record collection, citing legal, privacy and effectiveness concerns. The report includes separate statements by two members.
sources.reliability_and_relevance_notes: This is an oversight board’s conclusion, not a criminal judgement. Separate statements require substantive reading; assess existing court authorisations, inherited arrangements and Obama’s response.
sources.locator: Printed page 16, Recommendation 1; introduction and annex contents

sources.title: Remarks by the President on Review of Signals Intelligence
sources.author_or_issuing_institution: Barack Obama; Office of the Press Secretary
sources.factual_summary: Obama set out announced intelligence reforms and further privacy work, presenting the need to balance security and civil liberties.
sources.reliability_and_relevance_notes: Primary account of announced policy, not independent proof of implementation. It precedes the PCLOB report; do not describe it as a response to that report.
sources.locator: Speech, reform proposals and closing discussion of privacy review

sources.title: Remarks by the President at Sandy Hook Interfaith Prayer Vigil
sources.author_or_issuing_institution: Barack Obama; Office of the Press Secretary
sources.factual_summary: At the Newtown vigil Obama acknowledged bereaved families, praised responders and community support, and committed to work on preventing further shootings.
sources.reliability_and_relevance_notes: Evidence of public communication at one event. Seek family perspectives and follow-up actions; eloquence does not establish consistent empathy or successful prevention.
sources.locator: Speech at Newtown High School, passages on families and prevention

sources.title: Public Law 111–148 — Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act
sources.factual_summary: The catalogue identifies the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act as Public Law 111–148, dated 23 March 2010.
sources.reliability_and_relevance_notes: The catalogue establishes the legislative record. The statute, implementation and distributional effects have not been fully reviewed. Passing legislation is not automatically evidence of service or sound process.
sources.locator: Content Details

sources.title: Obama’s Numbers October 2016 Update
sources.factual_summary: The analysis reports changes in health insurance coverage and other indicators, and warns that numerical changes do not determine presidential credit or blame.
sources.reliability_and_relevance_notes: Follow links to original Census and NHIS data. Definitions and measurement periods differ. Outcomes provide context rather than direct measures of the six leadership dimensions.
sources.locator: Analysis introduction and Health Insurance section

sources.title: New Federal Government in office
sources.factual_summary: The government records Scholz’s election, appointment and oath as Federal Chancellor on 8 December 2021.
sources.reliability_and_relevance_notes: Chronology only. The oath does not establish fulfilment of the duties it describes.
sources.locator: Change of government; Bundestag elects Scholz; oath

sources.title: Bundeskanzler Friedrich Merz übernimmt Amtsgeschäfte
sources.factual_summary: The official record documents the handover from Scholz to Merz on 6 May 2025 and includes their statements.
sources.reliability_and_relevance_notes: A documented transfer and ceremonial words are relevant but cannot alone establish consistent humility or service. Check transition decisions and the wider record.
sources.locator: Dated introduction and handover statements

sources.title: Policy statement by Olaf Scholz, 27 February 2022 in Berlin
sources.factual_summary: Scholz announced a security-policy shift following Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, including a defence fund, commitments to allies and measures on energy security and household pressures.
sources.reliability_and_relevance_notes: Official English translation, not independent delivery evidence. Check the German transcript for contested wording and budgets, procurement and implementation for results.
sources.locator: Fourth policy area: defence capability; energy security and relief package

sources.title: Second Supplementary Budget Act 2021 is void
sources.factual_summary: Discovery lead for the Court’s account of its supplementary-budget judgement.
sources.reliability_and_relevance_notes: Direct retrieval failed with HTTP 403. Search snippets are not admitted as verified claims. Retrieve the judgement and government submissions before drawing a leader-specific conclusion.
sources.locator: Press release 101/2023; case 2 BvF 1/22

sources.title: German court deals 60 billion euro budget blow to Scholz government
sources.factual_summary: Reuters reported the budget ruling’s consequences and recorded Scholz’s stated intention to revise the relevant economic plan.
sources.reliability_and_relevance_notes: The host displays initial publication on 14 November and update on 15 November, with no explicit timezone. The judgement date is 15 November. This is a separately reviewed secondary account; the original court text remains outstanding. Multiple syndications are one source origin.
sources.locator: Updated 15 November 2023; report opening and Scholz response

sources.locator: Government posts: 24 July 2019–6 September 2022

sources.locator: Dated letter to Chief Constable Watson, copied to mayor and deputy; final decision paragraphs

anchors: will be removed from the ‘engage’ phase
sources.factual_summary: Supporting institutional record; see verification-01 for bounded use.

sources.title: Judgment of 15 November 2023 — 2 BvF 1/22
sources.locator: Operative judgement, preceding Reasons
sources.reliability_and_relevance_notes: Official English version. The invalidity of the legislation does not establish criminality or personal motives.
sources.factual_summary: Supporting institutional record; see verification-01 for bounded use.

sources.title: Prime Minister — oral answers, 12 January 2022
sources.factual_summary: Johnson apologised, acknowledged public sacrifices and said he had believed the May 2020 garden gathering was a work event; he accepted that he should have acted differently.
sources.reliability_and_relevance_notes: The apology and explanation are recorded words, not proof that the explanation was correct; compare the privileges findings about in-period statements.
sources.locator: Opening answer and later work-event answers

sources.title: Letter from Lord Geidt to the Prime Minister, 17 December 2021
sources.factual_summary: Geidt criticised incomplete disclosure of messages relevant to the flat-refurbishment investigation and insufficient regard for his role; he distinguished that criticism from his earlier interests assessment.
sources.reliability_and_relevance_notes: Preserve the qualified finding rather than alleging that a bribe or personal corruption was proved. Publication is later than the letter date.
sources.locator: Disclosure, notification and annex discussion

sources.title: Advice from the Independent Adviser on Ministers’ Interests, December 2021
sources.reliability_and_relevance_notes: Catalogue used to locate the original correspondence, not as substantive evidence.
sources.locator: Documents list

sources.title: Boris Johnson’s final speech as Prime Minister
sources.factual_summary: Johnson thanked staff and the public, referred critically to the circumstances of succession and pledged support for Liz Truss and the new government.
sources.reliability_and_relevance_notes: Mixed observable communication; do not infer his private motives or validate achievement claims in the speech.
sources.locator: Final speech, succession and closing paragraphs

sources.title: Boris Johnson’s first speech as Prime Minister
sources.factual_summary: Johnson set out governing commitments in his first Downing Street speech.
sources.reliability_and_relevance_notes: A baseline for comparing promises with later decisions, not delivery evidence or proof of public-service motivation.
sources.locator: Opening governing programme and commitments

sources.title: Conduct of Rt Hon Boris Johnson: Final Report
sources.author_or_issuing_institution: House of Commons Committee of Privileges
sources.factual_summary: The full report sets out its finding about misleading the House, Johnson’s account and arguments, and its reasons for rejecting aspects of them.
sources.reliability_and_relevance_notes: Later committee conduct and sanctions must not be scored as premiership behaviour. Only relevant sections were reviewed, not every evidential attachment.
sources.locator: Conclusions and sections on what Johnson told the House; representations considered in report

sources.title: Annual Report of the Independent Adviser on Ministers’ Interests: May 2022
sources.factual_summary: Geidt raised the question of the Ministerial Code’s legal-compliance duty following the Prime Minister’s fixed penalty notice and called for a public explanation of the Prime Minister’s position.
sources.reliability_and_relevance_notes: A question and advice are not a concluded independent finding that the Code was breached. Original publication day is not established in this packet.
sources.locator: Preface: fixed penalty notice and public confidence in the Code

sources.title: Starmer pays back more than £6,000 worth of gifts amid donations row
sources.factual_summary: ITV reported Downing Street’s statement that Starmer had paid for gifts and hospitality and commissioned revised principles.
sources.reliability_and_relevance_notes: A reported official account, not audited banking evidence. Repayment does not erase acceptance or establish that every conflict was resolved.
sources.locator: Report and quoted Downing Street statement

sources.title: PM remarks at Immigration White Paper press conference
sources.factual_summary: Starmer used the phrase island of strangers in explaining his government’s immigration proposals.
sources.reliability_and_relevance_notes: Assess treatment of people and communication, not agreement with immigration restrictions. Later regret is a separate event.
sources.locator: Transcript paragraph containing island of strangers

sources.title: Starmer says he deeply regrets using island of strangers phrase
sources.factual_summary: The report quotes Starmer’s regret and explanation in his Observer interview.
sources.reliability_and_relevance_notes: One interview origin, not independent corroboration merely because it is syndicated. The original interview has now been retrieved as NKS09.
sources.locator: Reported interview quotations

sources.title: Keir Starmer’s final speech as Prime Minister
sources.factual_summary: Starmer announced his resignation, thanked staff and the public, credited collective work and pledged support for his successor.
sources.reliability_and_relevance_notes: Verifies words and announced transfer, not the speech’s claims about the economy, public services or other achievements.
sources.locator: Resignation, successor and concluding thanks

sources.title: Keir Starmer’s first speech as Prime Minister
sources.factual_summary: Starmer presented service and public trust as governing commitments in his first speech.
sources.reliability_and_relevance_notes: Rhetorical baseline only; subsequent behaviour and institutional decisions must supply the assessment.
sources.locator: Initial governing commitments

sources.title: Ending rough sleeping by 2020 — new Mayor puts words into action
sources.factual_summary: GMCA states that Burnham launched a homelessness fund as a first mayoral act and donated part of his salary.
sources.reliability_and_relevance_notes: Page timestamp is 13 December 2018, while the account describes the start of the mayoralty. Event timing is contextualised by NAB07. Do not call this an audited recurring donation record or assume the 2020 goal was met.
sources.locator: Opening paragraphs on fund and salary; displayed publication timestamp

sources.title: Statements from the Mayor and Deputy Mayor on the future of Greater Manchester Police
sources.factual_summary: Burnham’s statement acknowledged unacceptable lack of progress, said the report was accepted and victims apologised to, and announced changes in force leadership.
sources.reliability_and_relevance_notes: Direct record of acknowledgement and announced action. It does not by itself establish adequate prior oversight or completed reform.
sources.locator: Mayor’s statement on report acceptance, apology and leadership

sources.title: Andy Burnham apologises for Manchester police homophobia
sources.reliability_and_relevance_notes: Direct retrieval returned HTTP 403. Record as unavailable primary/recipient material; the separate news account NAB06 was retrieved.
sources.locator: Letter and recipient account

sources.title: Declarations of interest — GMCA meeting of 27 September 2024
sources.factual_summary: The meeting record states that Burnham registered an interest concerning LEVI funding under the capital-funding item.
sources.reliability_and_relevance_notes: A narrow instance of disclosure. Do not infer a personal financial conflict, recusal or consistent compliance from it; publication date is not stated.
sources.locator: Decision under Declarations of Interest, Item 3

sources.title: Mayor and Deputy Mayor announce actions relating to HMICFRS report into GMP
sources.factual_summary: The statement accepted serious inspection issues and announced measures including a dedicated route for victims whose crimes were not recorded or appropriately handled.
sources.reliability_and_relevance_notes: Announced steps require follow-up. Distinguish the force-data reference period from the later inspection dates and the mayor’s own responsibilities.
sources.locator: Report response and victim hotline paragraphs

sources.title: Statement on the deaths of Warren Weinstein and Giovanni Lo Porto
sources.factual_summary: Obama accepted responsibility for counterterrorism operations, apologised to the families and described review of the operation that killed the hostages.
sources.reliability_and_relevance_notes: An acknowledgement of grave harm is relevant; it does not erase harm, prove the adequacy of safeguards or establish full accountability for every operation.
sources.locator: Statement paragraphs on responsibility, apology and review

sources.title: The President’s News Conference, 14 November 2013
sources.author_or_issuing_institution: Barack Obama; Office of the Federal Register
sources.factual_summary: Obama accepted responsibility for the health-law rollout, acknowledged loss of credibility and discussed corrective action.
sources.reliability_and_relevance_notes: Read alongside GAO’s independent findings and later follow-up; statements about repair are not evidence that every defect was resolved.
sources.locator: DCPD-201300781, printed page 4 and subsequent health-marketplace answers

sources.title: President Obama speaks on the results of the election
sources.author_or_issuing_institution: Barack Obama; White House transcript reproduced in blog
sources.factual_summary: Obama congratulated the president-elect and instructed his team to work towards a successful peaceful transition.
sources.reliability_and_relevance_notes: Observable communication and instruction, not confirmation of every transition action or acceptance of every substantive policy of the successor.
sources.locator: Reproduced speech paragraphs on call, team instructions and transition

sources.title: Executive Order 13490 — Ethics Commitments by Executive Branch Personnel
sources.factual_summary: The order requires an ethics pledge for appointees and contains restrictions, administration provisions and a written-waiver mechanism.
sources.reliability_and_relevance_notes: Instituted rules do not establish personal sacrifice, universal compliance or improper use of waivers. The waiver mechanism must not be omitted from a favourable account.
sources.locator: Pledge, section 3 Waiver and administration provisions

sources.title: Regierungserklärung zur Haushaltslage, 28 November 2023
sources.factual_summary: Scholz accepted the constitutional court decision as politically binding, described adjustments and framed the implications in terms of crisis management.
sources.reliability_and_relevance_notes: English summaries are research paraphrases of German. Acceptance is observable; the speech does not undo invalid budgeting or independently establish programme effectiveness.
sources.locator: Opening court-response passages

sources.title: Rede zur Entlassung des Bundesministers der Finanzen
sources.factual_summary: Scholz announced the finance minister’s dismissal, attributed serious failings to Lindner and proposed a confidence vote to enable an election.
sources.reliability_and_relevance_notes: Allegations about Lindner are Scholz’s position, not established facts here. Coalition and constitutional constraints matter; neither dismissal nor remaining in office proves ambition over service.
sources.locator: Reasons for dismissal and intended confidence timetable

sources.title: Vertrauensfrage und vorzeitige Neuwahlen
sources.factual_summary: The Bundestag records Scholz’s Article 68 confidence motion and its defeat on 16 December 2024.
sources.reliability_and_relevance_notes: The outcome is not a popularity or leadership-quality measure; relevance lies in use of the constitutional procedure.
sources.locator: Motion, vote result and constitutional procedure

sources.title: Reaktionen auf die Hochrechnungen zur Bundestagswahl
sources.factual_summary: The report records Scholz accepting responsibility for his party’s result and saying he would carry out his duties until the last day.
sources.reliability_and_relevance_notes: The election outcome itself is excluded from scoring. An attributed acceptance is not independent proof of broad self-correction.
sources.locator: Scholz response to early election results

sources.title: Scholz zur Haushaltskrise: Eine neue Realität und kein konkreter Fahrplan
sources.factual_summary: The analysis notes that the budget statement did not include an apology and criticises its lack of a concrete timetable.

claims.text: The Committee concluded that Johnson deliberately misled the House. The summary records its reasoning, his denials and his response to provisional conclusions.
claims.locator: Summary, paragraphs 11–17
claims.verification_note: The summary supports the attributed Committee conclusion. June 2023 committee conduct is outside the premiership. Full representations and Commons disposition remain outside this bounded verification.

claims.text: The committees identified both vaccination successes and serious weaknesses in the early pandemic response, including delayed lockdown and shortcomings affecting vulnerable groups.
claims.locator: Opening summary and principal findings
claims.verification_note: Both strengths and weaknesses are present in the official inquiry announcement. This verifies the summary, not all claims in the full report or personal prime ministerial responsibility.

claims.text: The government recorded Johnson’s Kyiv visit and announced additional military assistance and World Bank lending guarantees.
claims.locator: Paragraphs describing assistance and lending guarantees
claims.verification_note: The announcement records military aid and guarantees. Delivery and effect have not been independently established by this release.

claims.text: The retrieved biography states that Starmer was Prime Minister from 5 July 2024 to 20 July 2026.
claims.locator: Biography
claims.verification_note: Both boundaries agree with UK Parliament career record V02. This is cross-checking two institutional records, not certification of every biography statement.

claims.text: The announcement sets out monthly publication of ministerial gifts and hospitality, including values, and an independent adviser’s power to initiate investigations without a prime ministerial veto.
claims.locator: Gifts and hospitality rules; independent adviser powers
claims.verification_note: The dated announcement supports monthly disclosure and the no-veto investigation provision. Enforcement and actual compliance remain unverified.

claims.text: The register includes Arsenal tickets and hospitality received on 17 August 2024 and declared on 10 September 2024. Other entries concern earlier dates or periods straddling the start of the premiership.
claims.locator: Category 3; Arsenal entry received 17 August 2024; accommodation entry 29 May–13 July 2024
claims.verification_note: The Arsenal entry confirms receipt/acceptance on 17 August and registration on 10 September. Other benefits predate office or straddle it; no breach finding is inferred.

claims.text: The publication record identifies the Plan for Change and states it was presented to Parliament on 5 December 2024.
claims.locator: Details and document metadata: CP 1210, ISBN 978-1-5286-5291-9
claims.verification_note: Publication date, CP number and presentation to Parliament are confirmed on the landing page. The attachment is not represented as substantively reviewed.

claims.text: Starmer condemned violent disorder, referred to targeted Muslim and other minority communities, and stated that the government would support the police and pursue criminal enforcement.
claims.locator: Speech transcript, paragraphs on targeted communities and policing
claims.verification_note: The transcript supports the limited description of words delivered. Operational outcomes and effects on communities remain outside this source’s proof.

claims.text: The Treasury announced expanded Winter Fuel Payment eligibility in England and Wales using a £35,000 income threshold, following the narrower arrangements introduced for winter 2024/25.
claims.locator: Eligibility announcement and Further background
claims.verification_note: Treasury announcement confirms the threshold and the narrower 2024/25 background. Attribution to Starmer’s personal reasoning remains unsupported.

claims.text: The inspection identified serious weaknesses in victim service, crime recording, investigation and governance, while recognising some improvements and a programme of change.
claims.locator: Printed pages 8–12: summary, supervision and governance, causes of concern; inspection conducted September–October 2020
claims.verification_note: The report confirms the September–October 2020 inspection and adverse as well as qualifying findings. Footer confirms December 2020, but an exact publication day is not established.

claims.text: The police force announced removal from enhanced monitoring and described improvements in call handling, recording and investigation.
claims.locator: Opening announcement and crime-recording/investigation passages
claims.verification_note: The institutional account is now corroborated on the narrow removal-from-monitoring decision by the inspector’s original letter V05. Other performance figures and personal credit remain separately unverified.

claims.text: The archival biography records Obama’s inauguration on 20 January 2009 and return to private life on 20 January 2017.
claims.locator: Political Career and Post-Presidency
claims.verification_note: Only the inauguration and return-to-private-life dates were used. No other biographical claim is admitted through this verification.

claims.text: GAO identified inadequate CMS planning and oversight, increased contract costs and delayed functionality. The record includes agency responses and later implementation of recommendations.
claims.locator: What GAO Found; Recommendations for Executive Action
claims.verification_note: GAO highlights confirm planning and oversight weaknesses, cost increases and delayed functionality. Dynamic follow-up records implemented recommendations; that is separate from the 2014 original finding.

claims.text: The Board recommended ending bulk telephone-record collection, citing legal, privacy and effectiveness concerns. The report includes separate statements by two members.
claims.locator: Printed page 16, Recommendation 1; introduction and annex contents
claims.verification_note: Recommendation 1 supports the attributed legal/privacy/value concerns; contents identify separate member statements. They must be read before treating the conclusions as unanimous. This is not a judicial criminal finding.

claims.text: Obama set out announced intelligence reforms and further privacy work, presenting the need to balance security and civil liberties.
claims.locator: Speech, reform proposals and closing discussion of privacy review
claims.verification_note: Reform announcements and privacy work are in the 17 January speech. The speech predates the 23 January PCLOB report and is not described as a response to it.

claims.text: At the Newtown vigil Obama acknowledged bereaved families, praised responders and community support, and committed to work on preventing further shootings.
claims.locator: Speech at Newtown High School, passages on families and prevention
claims.verification_note: Transcript confirms the limited account of acknowledgement, praise and commitments. Empathy over the whole term and prevention outcomes are not established.

claims.text: The catalogue identifies the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act as Public Law 111–148, dated 23 March 2010.
claims.locator: Content Details
claims.verification_note: GovInfo catalogue confirms law identifier and 23 March 2010 date. No substantive statutory or implementation conclusion is inferred from metadata.

claims.text: The analysis reports changes in health insurance coverage and other indicators, and warns that numerical changes do not determine presidential credit or blame.
claims.locator: Analysis introduction and Health Insurance section
claims.verification_note: The analysis discusses insurance indicators and explicitly cautions against automatic presidential credit/blame. Original datasets and causal attribution remain outstanding.

claims.text: The government records Scholz’s election, appointment and oath as Federal Chancellor on 8 December 2021.
claims.locator: Change of government; Bundestag elects Scholz; oath
claims.verification_note: Official dated appointment/oath record supports 8 December 2021. An oath is not evidence that every duty was fulfilled.

claims.text: The official record documents the handover from Scholz to Merz on 6 May 2025 and includes their statements.
claims.locator: Dated introduction and handover statements
claims.verification_note: Dated handover record supports 6 May 2025 and observable transfer conduct. Ceremonial statements do not establish consistent humility.

claims.text: Scholz announced a security-policy shift following Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, including a defence fund, commitments to allies and measures on energy security and household pressures.
claims.locator: Fourth policy area: defence capability; energy security and relief package
claims.verification_note: Official English text supports the announced defence fund, allied commitments and energy/household measures. Delivery is not established. German wording still requires review for any contested phrase.

claims.text: Reuters reported the budget ruling’s consequences and recorded Scholz’s stated intention to revise the relevant economic plan.
claims.locator: Updated 15 November 2023; report opening and Scholz response
claims.verification_note: Byline, displayed initial/update dates and quoted plan revision are confirmed. The underlying ruling is now checked against OS04 and V06; multiple syndicated versions would not count as independent origins.

claims.text: The GMCA notice states that the mayoral vacancy occurred on 19 June 2026 after Burnham’s election as an MP.
claims.locator: Vacancy notice, published 19 June 2026
claims.verification_note: Previously inaccessible page now retrieved directly. It gives the vacancy date as 19 June 2026 and was published that day. The start date is separately supported by V03.

claims.text: The independent review records that Burnham commissioned it and prioritised the experiences of bereaved families and other affected people.
claims.locator: Sections 1.2–1.3, printed pages 11–12
claims.verification_note: PDF now retrieved. Sections 1.2–1.3 establish commissioning and intended family participation. Section 2.22 records positive visit experiences; section 2.23 records perceived geographical gaps in support. These accounts do not establish representativeness or sole mayoral responsibility.

claims.text: The report records some respondents’ positive accounts of personal visits by the mayor and chief constable.
claims.locator: Section 2.22, printed pages 49–50
claims.verification_note: PDF now retrieved. Sections 1.2–1.3 establish commissioning and intended family participation. Section 2.22 records positive visit experiences; section 2.23 records perceived geographical gaps in support. These accounts do not establish representativeness or sole mayoral responsibility.

claims.text: The report also records that some respondents outside Manchester felt overlooked or less well supported. This is not a finding of Burnham’s sole responsibility.
claims.locator: Section 2.23, printed page 50
claims.verification_note: PDF now retrieved. Sections 1.2–1.3 establish commissioning and intended family participation. Section 2.22 records positive visit experiences; section 2.23 records perceived geographical gaps in support. These accounts do not establish representativeness or sole mayoral responsibility.

claims.text: GMCA records Burnham’s decision to introduce bus franchising in March 2021, with the first services running in September 2023 and final rollout in January 2025.
claims.locator: The journey to franchised bus services
claims.verification_note: Official overview now retrieved. It records the March 2021 decision and rollout dates. Its budget, patronage and comparative claims are not independently validated here.

claims.text: The Court’s press release states that the Second Supplementary Budget Act 2021 was incompatible with specified Basic Law provisions and void; the operative judgement confirms this.
claims.locator: Press release opening; V06 operative judgement
claims.verification_note: Previously inaccessible press release now retrieved. Its operative account agrees with the separately retrieved judgement V06. Invalid legislation is not a finding of personal dishonesty.

claims.text: Johnson apologised, acknowledged public sacrifices and said he had believed the May 2020 garden gathering was a work event; he accepted that he should have acted differently.
claims.locator: Opening answer and later work-event answers
claims.limitations: The apology and explanation are recorded words, not proof that the explanation was correct; compare the privileges findings about in-period statements.

claims.text: Geidt criticised incomplete disclosure of messages relevant to the flat-refurbishment investigation and insufficient regard for his role; he distinguished that criticism from his earlier interests assessment.
claims.locator: Disclosure, notification and annex discussion
claims.limitations: Preserve the qualified finding rather than alleging that a bribe or personal corruption was proved. Publication is later than the letter date.

claims.text: Johnson thanked staff and the public, referred critically to the circumstances of succession and pledged support for Liz Truss and the new government.
claims.locator: Final speech, succession and closing paragraphs
claims.limitations: Mixed observable communication; do not infer his private motives or validate achievement claims in the speech.

claims.text: Johnson set out governing commitments in his first Downing Street speech.
claims.locator: Opening governing programme and commitments
claims.limitations: A baseline for comparing promises with later decisions, not delivery evidence or proof of public-service motivation.

claims.text: The full report sets out its finding about misleading the House, Johnson’s account and arguments, and its reasons for rejecting aspects of them.
claims.locator: Conclusions and sections on what Johnson told the House; representations considered in report
claims.limitations: Later committee conduct and sanctions must not be scored as premiership behaviour. Only relevant sections were reviewed, not every evidential attachment.

claims.text: Geidt raised the question of the Ministerial Code’s legal-compliance duty following the Prime Minister’s fixed penalty notice and called for a public explanation of the Prime Minister’s position.
claims.locator: Preface: fixed penalty notice and public confidence in the Code
claims.limitations: A question and advice are not a concluded independent finding that the Code was breached. Original publication day is not established in this packet.

claims.text: ITV reported Downing Street’s statement that Starmer had paid for gifts and hospitality and commissioned revised principles.
claims.locator: Report and quoted Downing Street statement
claims.limitations: A reported official account, not audited banking evidence. Repayment does not erase acceptance or establish that every conflict was resolved.

claims.text: Starmer used the phrase island of strangers in explaining his government’s immigration proposals.
claims.locator: Transcript paragraph containing island of strangers
claims.limitations: Assess treatment of people and communication, not agreement with immigration restrictions. Later regret is a separate event.

claims.text: The report quotes Starmer’s regret and explanation in his Observer interview.
claims.locator: Reported interview quotations
claims.limitations: One interview origin, not independent corroboration merely because it is syndicated. The original interview has now been retrieved as NKS09.

claims.text: Starmer announced his resignation, thanked staff and the public, credited collective work and pledged support for his successor.
claims.locator: Resignation, successor and concluding thanks
claims.limitations: Verifies words and announced transfer, not the speech’s claims about the economy, public services or other achievements.

claims.text: Starmer presented service and public trust as governing commitments in his first speech.
claims.locator: Initial governing commitments
claims.limitations: Rhetorical baseline only; subsequent behaviour and institutional decisions must supply the assessment.

claims.text: GMCA states that Burnham launched a homelessness fund as a first mayoral act and donated part of his salary.
claims.locator: Opening paragraphs on fund and salary; displayed publication timestamp
claims.limitations: Page timestamp is 13 December 2018, while the account describes the start of the mayoralty. Event timing is contextualised by NAB07. Do not call this an audited recurring donation record or assume the 2020 goal was met.

claims.text: Burnham’s statement acknowledged unacceptable lack of progress, said the report was accepted and victims apologised to, and announced changes in force leadership.
claims.locator: Mayor’s statement on report acceptance, apology and leadership
claims.limitations: Direct record of acknowledgement and announced action. It does not by itself establish adequate prior oversight or completed reform.

claims.text: The meeting record states that Burnham registered an interest concerning LEVI funding under the capital-funding item.
claims.locator: Decision under Declarations of Interest, Item 3
claims.limitations: A narrow instance of disclosure. Do not infer a personal financial conflict, recusal or consistent compliance from it; publication date is not stated.

claims.text: The statement accepted serious inspection issues and announced measures including a dedicated route for victims whose crimes were not recorded or appropriately handled.
claims.locator: Report response and victim hotline paragraphs
claims.limitations: Announced steps require follow-up. Distinguish the force-data reference period from the later inspection dates and the mayor’s own responsibilities.

claims.text: Obama accepted responsibility for counterterrorism operations, apologised to the families and described review of the operation that killed the hostages.
claims.locator: Statement paragraphs on responsibility, apology and review
claims.limitations: An acknowledgement of grave harm is relevant; it does not erase harm, prove the adequacy of safeguards or establish full accountability for every operation.

claims.text: Obama accepted responsibility for the health-law rollout, acknowledged loss of credibility and discussed corrective action.
claims.locator: DCPD-201300781, printed page 4 and subsequent health-marketplace answers
claims.limitations: Read alongside GAO’s independent findings and later follow-up; statements about repair are not evidence that every defect was resolved.

claims.text: Obama congratulated the president-elect and instructed his team to work towards a successful peaceful transition.
claims.locator: Reproduced speech paragraphs on call, team instructions and transition
claims.limitations: Observable communication and instruction, not confirmation of every transition action or acceptance of every substantive policy of the successor.

claims.text: The order requires an ethics pledge for appointees and contains restrictions, administration provisions and a written-waiver mechanism.
claims.locator: Pledge, section 3 Waiver and administration provisions
claims.limitations: Instituted rules do not establish personal sacrifice, universal compliance or improper use of waivers. The waiver mechanism must not be omitted from a favourable account.

claims.text: Scholz accepted the constitutional court decision as politically binding, described adjustments and framed the implications in terms of crisis management.
claims.locator: Opening court-response passages
claims.limitations: English summaries are research paraphrases of German. Acceptance is observable; the speech does not undo invalid budgeting or independently establish programme effectiveness.

claims.text: Scholz announced the finance minister’s dismissal, attributed serious failings to Lindner and proposed a confidence vote to enable an election.
claims.locator: Reasons for dismissal and intended confidence timetable
claims.limitations: Allegations about Lindner are Scholz’s position, not established facts here. Coalition and constitutional constraints matter; neither dismissal nor remaining in office proves ambition over service.

claims.text: The Bundestag records Scholz’s Article 68 confidence motion and its defeat on 16 December 2024.
claims.locator: Motion, vote result and constitutional procedure
claims.limitations: The outcome is not a popularity or leadership-quality measure; relevance lies in use of the constitutional procedure.

claims.text: The report records Scholz accepting responsibility for his party’s result and saying he would carry out his duties until the last day.
claims.locator: Scholz response to early election results
claims.limitations: The election outcome itself is excluded from scoring. An attributed acceptance is not independent proof of broad self-correction.

claims.text: The analysis notes that the budget statement did not include an apology and criticises its lack of a concrete timetable.
claims.locator: Sections on timetable and Keine Entschuldigung
claims.limitations: Labelled analytical interpretation, not a new legal finding or proof of personality. Use with the original speech NOS01.

claims.text: Johnson apologised for the adviser’s position and incomplete explanation, defended parts of his office’s handling and proposed more support and information access for the adviser.
claims.locator: Letter paragraphs on apology, disclosure and proposed steps
claims.limitations: Direct acknowledgement and promises; implementation is not established. Read alongside Geidt rather than treating the response as an exoneration.

claims.text: The Plan sets out named milestones and numerical targets and presents them as a basis for public accountability.
claims.locator: Foreword and milestone list, printed pages 5–7; chapter headings
claims.limitations: Relevant sections of the 48-page PDF reviewed. Targets and institutional reform intentions are not achieved outcomes; no full-document implementation audit claimed.

claims.text: The report quotes Burnham’s letter apologising for historical discrimination, his statement about operational independence and Tatchell’s view that a mayoral apology did not replace a force apology.
claims.locator: Quoted letter and recipient response
claims.limitations: Original letter not retrieved here. The mayor’s 2025 acknowledgement is in period; the historical abuses described are not attributed to his own mayoralty.

claims.text: The study describes citizen participation in the Foreign Office’s strategy process and argues that control techniques limited its opening.
claims.locator: German and English abstracts
claims.limitations: The study concerns a Foreign Office process, not a finding of Scholz’s individual empathy or manipulation. Issue year is 2025; online publication is 20 June 2024.

claims.text: DWP reports recipients under changed eligibility and explains comparisons with earlier winters.
claims.locator: Main stories and eligibility/comparability notes
claims.limitations: Retrospective source about an in-period winter. Counts, recipients and beneficiaries differ; this is context, not proof of Starmer’s personal listening or a moral score.

claims.text: The interview reports Burnham’s salary pledge and questions him about homelessness, mental health and how support would work.
claims.locator: Introduction and interview questions on the homelessness fund
claims.limitations: Directly questioned commitments, not bank records or measured results; charity-focused publication has an explicit public-interest perspective.

claims.text: The strategy connects national-security and international-policy objectives to priority actions to 2025 in a strategic framework.
claims.locator: Introduction and Strategic Framework
claims.limitations: Accessible text updated 2 July 2021; original publication day not established by this file alone. This establishes an articulated strategy, not coherent delivery across all policy.

claims.text: In the original interview Starmer regretted the phrase, said he had not intended the historical echo and acknowledged that he should have scrutinised the speech more carefully.
claims.locator: Interview passage discussing the May immigration speech
claims.limitations: Original published interview, not unedited recording. It establishes an attributed acknowledgement and explanation, not that the explanation is independently proved.

claims.text: Rachel Brand’s separate statement disagrees with ending the telephone-record programme without an adequate alternative and supports many other recommendations.
claims.locator: Annex A, printed pages 208–213
claims.limitations: Dissent is not an exoneration. Preserve majority and separate reasoning without counting members as source votes.

claims.text: Elisebeth Collins Cook’s separate statement supports modifications but disputes the report’s statutory-authorisation, constitutional and efficacy analyses.
claims.locator: Annex B, printed pages 214–218
claims.limitations: Dissent is not an exoneration. Preserve majority and separate reasoning without counting members as source votes.

claims.text: In his 17 December 2021 letter, Geidt maintained the fundamental assessment that the payment did not create a conflict or reasonably perceived conflict, while qualifying other conclusions and criticising disclosure.
claims.locator: Letter opening: impact on earlier advice; subsequent disclosure sections
claims.limitations: A specific finding about the interests created by this payment, not general exoneration of all conduct or a finding that the investigation received full disclosure.

dimensions.draft_judgement: Johnson acknowledged public sacrifices in his January 2022 apology. That records citizen-facing communication. The packet does not yet establish a sustained pattern of listening influencing his decisions; pandemic findings require a personal decision trail, and the Ukraine announcement does not supply that missing link.
dimensions.uncertainties: Acknowledgement is not documented listening into decisions; collective pandemic outcomes require an individual decision trail. Affected-community testimony and routine consultation remain underrepresented.
dimensions.score_withholding_reason: Material coverage, attribution or interpretation gaps described above remain unresolved. A number would imply a whole-period judgement not yet supported.
dimensions.internal_review_reason: BJ05-C1 is a policy announcement, not direct evidence of empathy or listening. BJ04-C1 concerns collective pandemic performance. Keep those forms of evidence separate.

dimensions.draft_judgement: The prorogation judgement and the Committee’s finding about in-period statements supply specific adverse institutional evidence. Geidt criticised disclosure but maintained his narrow no-conflict assessment concerning the payment. Johnson’s apology and proposed support are relevant recorded responses; the departure speech establishes stated support for succession, not verification of every transfer action.
dimensions.uncertainties: The conduct dates underlying the 2023 report must be separated from the later inquiry behaviour. The rubric has no approved rule for balancing severe violations against ordinary compliance.
dimensions.score_withholding_reason: Material coverage, attribution or interpretation gaps described above remain unresolved. A number would imply a whole-period judgement not yet supported.
dimensions.internal_review_reason: The phrase announced lawful transfer promotes a speech into verified lawful conduct. The qualified Geidt finding must also be visible alongside the disclosure criticism.

dimensions.draft_judgement: An articulated strategic direction is documented in the Integrated Review and Ukraine-support announcements. Pandemic weaknesses qualify the broader claim that direction was consistently supported by disciplined implementation.
dimensions.uncertainties: Cross-domain delivery, resources and justified revisions require fuller checking. Strategy rhetoric cannot be treated as achieved consistency; ideological agreement is excluded.
dimensions.score_withholding_reason: Material coverage, attribution or interpretation gaps described above remain unresolved. A number would imply a whole-period judgement not yet supported.
dimensions.internal_review_reason: The paragraph distinguishes articulated strategy from implementation and excludes ideological agreement. Its stated delivery gaps properly prevent a whole-period score.

dimensions.draft_judgement: The packet records announced Ukraine support and mixed findings about the pandemic response. These are relevant cases for further inquiry, but the present evidence does not establish Johnson’s composure, communication of uncertainty or individual decision quality across the assessed period.
dimensions.uncertainties: The current amended Covid Inquiry Volume I could not be downloaded (NBJ10, HTTP 503). Individual responsibility and communication of uncertainty remain material gaps.
dimensions.score_withholding_reason: Material coverage, attribution or interpretation gaps described above remain unresolved. A number would imply a whole-period judgement not yet supported.
dimensions.internal_review_reason: A pledge of aid and a collective pandemic assessment do not establish personal composure or calm communication across crises. The summary overstates the available construct-specific evidence.

dimensions.draft_judgement: There are direct acknowledgements and apologies, so a claim that Johnson never admitted error would be unsustainable. Their scope and adequacy are qualified by the adviser’s concerns and the Committee’s findings about his explanations.
dimensions.uncertainties: Assess the original words rather than inferred sincerity. Later committee behaviour is outside the scored office period; subsequent implementation of promised corrections is incompletely documented.
dimensions.score_withholding_reason: Material coverage, attribution or interpretation gaps described above remain unresolved. A number would imply a whole-period judgement not yet supported.
dimensions.internal_review_reason: Direct apologies are appropriately qualified by the adviser and parliamentary findings; the draft does not infer sincerity or assign a numerical score.

dimensions.draft_judgement: The refurbishment correspondence establishes serious disclosure concerns and also Geidt’s maintained, specific no-conflict assessment about the payment. Those findings must be weighed together. Proposed safeguards and statements about succession are documented, but the packet does not establish a general pattern of choosing public duty over personal advantage.
dimensions.uncertainties: Do not convert an interests concern into a proved bribe or claim that leaving office alone demonstrates selflessness. Relevant declarations, original qualified findings and follow-up must all be weighed.
dimensions.score_withholding_reason: Material coverage, attribution or interpretation gaps described above remain unresolved. A number would imply a whole-period judgement not yet supported.
dimensions.internal_review_reason: The specific maintained no-conflict assessment is material contrary evidence and should appear in the judgement, rather than only in source notes. Transfer statements remain statements.

dimensions.draft_judgement: The record combines explicit concern for targeted communities with language later acknowledged as a mistake. The later acknowledgement provides evidence of correction, while the original communication remains material to citizen focus.
dimensions.uncertainties: Community experience and decisions resulting from listening require further evidence. Benefit-recipient statistics describe reach, not empathy or Starmer’s individual reasons.
dimensions.score_withholding_reason: Material coverage, attribution or interpretation gaps described above remain unresolved. A number would imply a whole-period judgement not yet supported.
dimensions.internal_review_reason: The draft keeps the initial language and subsequent acknowledgement together without treating policy agreement or benefit counts as empathy.

dimensions.draft_judgement: The dated register documents declarations, and the government announcement describes proposed transparency and investigatory changes. Reported repayment supplies a related benefits-management case. The packet does not establish consistent compliance or enforcement; the historical code-version conflict remains unresolved.
dimensions.uncertainties: No claim of consistent enforcement is supported. The purported November 2024 PDF returns an October 2025 title (NKS07); historical code text and enforcement records remain unresolved.
dimensions.score_withholding_reason: Material coverage, attribution or interpretation gaps described above remain unresolved. A number would imply a whole-period judgement not yet supported.
dimensions.internal_review_reason: Reported repayment is not itself institutional transparency, and published targets principally address Policy. Keep the Process judgement anchored to rules, disclosures and enforcement.

dimensions.draft_judgement: The Plan for Change supplies inspectable targets rather than only an opening speech. The benefits revision is a relevant adaptation case, but its merits depend on reasons, implementation and context rather than the fact of reversal alone.
dimensions.uncertainties: The packet does not establish fulfilment of the whole strategy or resource alignment. Later public-service success claims in the resignation speech are excluded from verified outcomes.
dimensions.score_withholding_reason: Material coverage, attribution or interpretation gaps described above remain unresolved. A number would imply a whole-period judgement not yet supported.
dimensions.internal_review_reason: The paragraph accurately separates targets, adaptation and implementation. The reasons for the benefits revision remain open rather than automatically scored as inconsistency.

dimensions.draft_judgement: The disorder transcript records Starmer’s stated support for targeted communities, police and legal enforcement. It does not by itself establish protection achieved, personal composure or effective coordination. The immigration speech is retained as communication evidence under People and Humility; its inclusion as a crisis case requires a demonstrated connection to acute crisis decision-making.
dimensions.uncertainties: Do not equate emphatic language with either composure or its absence. Operational records, independent evaluations and decisions during the latter part of the term are insufficiently covered.
dimensions.score_withholding_reason: Material coverage, attribution or interpretation gaps described above remain unresolved. A number would imply a whole-period judgement not yet supported.
dimensions.internal_review_reason: Protecting targeted communities implies an achieved action when KS05 is a speech. The immigration speech is not automatically crisis evidence; a link to acute pressure needs separate support.

dimensions.draft_judgement: There is direct published acknowledgement that the immigration wording was wrong and should have received more scrutiny, alongside reported repayment and credit to others at departure. These are observable humility indicators, while the initial error remains part of the same case.
dimensions.uncertainties: The Observer is an edited published interview, and later articles are not independent evidence origins. Consistent acceptance of criticism and follow-through across the term remains unestablished.
dimensions.score_withholding_reason: Material coverage, attribution or interpretation gaps described above remain unresolved. A number would imply a whole-period judgement not yet supported.
dimensions.internal_review_reason: The original interview supports acknowledgement and acceptance of some personal responsibility. The draft preserves the initial error and the limits of an edited interview.

dimensions.draft_judgement: Reported repayment is a specific action concerning personal benefits, and the departure speech records support for the successor. Neither proves that all conflicts were avoided or that personal ambition never influenced decisions.
dimensions.uncertainties: Payment details are reported official statements rather than audited bank records. Accepting declared benefits remains relevant context but is not silently classified as misconduct.
dimensions.score_withholding_reason: Material coverage, attribution or interpretation gaps described above remain unresolved. A number would imply a whole-period judgement not yet supported.
dimensions.internal_review_reason: Reported repayment is explicitly attributed, while declarations and succession words are not used to establish the absence of conflicts or private ambition. The remaining gaps are material.

dimensions.draft_judgement: Family-centred commissioning, positive accounts of personal visits and responses to victim concerns provide direct evidence of attention to people. Geographical gaps reported by families and serious victim-service failures prevent a one-sided conclusion.
dimensions.uncertainties: Kerslake testimony is valuable but not a representative survey. Police-service failures must be connected to the mayor’s knowledge, powers and oversight rather than assigned personally by default.
dimensions.score_withholding_reason: Material coverage, attribution or interpretation gaps described above remain unresolved. A number would imply a whole-period judgement not yet supported.
dimensions.internal_review_reason: The draft uses direct family accounts and commissioning evidence with geographical and victim-service qualifications, and explicitly limits personal attribution.

dimensions.draft_judgement: The record contains review commissioning, a specific declared interest and a mayoral response to policing failures. V05 corroborates the force’s removal from enhanced monitoring while acknowledging remaining work. Whether the mayor’s oversight was timely and adequate before those failures is not yet established.
dimensions.uncertainties: A disclosed interest does not prove a financial conflict or recusal. Prior warnings, scrutiny, delegation and timeliness need fuller reconstruction before evaluating institutional discipline over nine years.
dimensions.score_withholding_reason: Material coverage, attribution or interpretation gaps described above remain unresolved. A number would imply a whole-period judgement not yet supported.
dimensions.internal_review_reason: Review commissioning, a single declaration and later organisational improvement do not demonstrate consistently adequate mayoral oversight. State the narrower institutional record.

dimensions.draft_judgement: Bus-franchising decision and rollout chronology provide a concrete strategic case. Homelessness pledges show a second direction but do not establish delivery; police weaknesses qualify any general claim of disciplined execution.
dimensions.uncertainties: Do not assume that the rough-sleeping deadline was met. Independent cost, service and homelessness outcomes are not sufficiently established, and organisational findings do not automatically become the mayor’s policy failure.
dimensions.score_withholding_reason: Material coverage, attribution or interpretation gaps described above remain unresolved. A number would imply a whole-period judgement not yet supported.
dimensions.internal_review_reason: The draft distinguishes rollout chronology and pledges from delivery, and does not assume the homelessness goal was achieved or assign all police failings personally.

dimensions.draft_judgement: The evidence documents review commissioning and subsequent victim-support and leadership announcements. It does not adequately establish Burnham’s composure or calm communication during the acute events. Original immediate-response records and a clearer personal decision chronology are required.
dimensions.uncertainties: The Arena review did not have statutory powers; subsequent inquiry findings and personal decision chronology remain necessary. A police apology for events before Burnham’s mayoralty is not evidence that he caused those events.
dimensions.score_withholding_reason: Material coverage, attribution or interpretation gaps described above remain unresolved. A number would imply a whole-period judgement not yet supported.

dimensions.draft_judgement: A contemporary interview records a salary pledge, while GMCA later describes a contribution with inconsistent publication/event dating. dimensions.uncertainties: The official donation page’s date conflicts with its first-act framing; contemporary interview corroborates the pledge, not all payments. No adverse personal-benefit finding has been established, which is not proof that none exists.

They do not yet establish sustained listening or responsiveness across both terms.
dimensions.uncertainties: Speeches are not a representative record of listening, and outcomes are not personal empathy measures. Family experience, civilian-harm records and original coverage data need deeper review.

dimensions.uncertainties: The Board was not unanimous on shutting down the programme or legal analysis. Ethical rules include waivers; neither their existence nor their mere availability establishes consistent conduct or abuse.

dimensions.internal_review_reason: The majority and separate PCLOB positions are distinguished, ethics waivers are retained and organisational audit conclusions are not treated as automatic personal misconduct.

dimensions.draft_judgement: The health-law record connects an enacted programme, implementation shortcomings and announced repairs. It is a suitable case for examining strategic direction and adaptation without deciding whether the ideology was desirable.
dimensions.uncertainties: Implementation after repair, resource choices, other policy domains and original datasets remain incomplete. Legislation and population trends are not interchangeable with policy coherence.

dimensions.internal_review_reason: The claim is a bounded case analysis, with legislation, implementation and proposed repairs kept distinct and no ideological or causal inference.

dimensions.draft_judgement: There are records of communication after tragedy and acceptance of responsibility during policy failure. They support analysis of those communications but do not establish Obama’s composure, handling of uncertainty or individual crisis decisions across both terms. The audit concerns implementation; hostage deaths remain adverse outcomes requiring their own responsibility analysis.
dimensions.uncertainties: Hostage deaths remain grave harm, not a positive event because an apology followed. Assess contemporary intelligence, safeguards and follow-up. Financial-crisis and other first-term decision records remain thin.
dimensions.score_withholding_reason: Material coverage, attribution or interpretation gaps described above remain unresolved. A number would imply a whole-period judgement not yet supported.
dimensions.internal_review_reason: Acknowledgement after an error and communication after tragedy do not by themselves establish composure in decision-making. The current draft leans towards a general crisis assessment without enough contemporaneous decision evidence.

dimensions.draft_judgement: Two different episodes document personal acceptance of responsibility, and the transition statement credits the predecessor’s example while supporting the successor. These are substantive observable humility indicators.
dimensions.uncertainties: Acknowledgement does not establish sincerity or adequate remedy. Selective transparency and unresolved contrary cases must be tested across both terms; the reviewed early-term personal-conduct sample remains limited.

dimensions.internal_review_reason: The two original acknowledgement episodes and credit to the predecessor directly support bounded observable indicators. The draft correctly refrains from diagnosing personality or scoring the whole period.

dimensions.draft_judgement: The ethics order, its waiver mechanism and transition instructions document institutional rules and stated duties. The packet has not established how Obama personally managed competing private interests or forewent advantage over the full period. Surveillance findings concern public duties and rights; they are not evidence of a personal-benefit motive.
dimensions.uncertainties: Do not score policy disagreement as self-interest, or ethical rules as proof of personal sacrifice. Conflicts disclosures, waiver practice and consistent management require further original records.

dimensions.internal_review_reason: Institutional ethics rules and a transition instruction are relevant duties but do not establish personal sacrifice or consistent interests management. Competing surveillance-policy arguments cannot fill the personal-benefit evidence gap.

dimensions.draft_judgement: The security speech records attention to household pressures as a stated aim. The participation study provides institutional context about a Foreign Office process. dimensions.uncertainties: The participation study concerns the Foreign Office, not proof of Scholz’s individual listening. Affected-community evidence and a direct decision-to-consultation trail remain insufficient.

dimensions.draft_judgement: The invalid supplementary budget is a concrete institutional failure. Public acceptance of the decision, use of a confidence procedure and documented transfer provide important countervailing evidence of working within constitutional processes.
dimensions.uncertainties: Acceptance after an adverse ruling does not erase it. Full submissions, legal advice and the allocation of responsibility inside the coalition require closer reading; do not infer dishonesty.

dimensions.internal_review_reason: Original invalidity, the subsequent response and constitutional procedure remain distinct; no dishonesty or electoral-quality inference is made.

dimensions.draft_judgement: The security statement articulates a policy shift. The invalid supplementary-budget instrument supplies a specific problem in matching financing to legal requirements. The budget response and coalition dispute identify further questions about resources and adaptation; coalition breakdown alone does not establish incoherent policy or deficient leadership.
dimensions.uncertainties: Delivery records and trade-offs remain incomplete. The external analysis of a missing timetable is commentary, not a new court finding or evidence that every strategic programme lacked direction.

dimensions.internal_review_reason: Coalition breakdown is not automatically policy incoherence, and a court-invalidated funding instrument should be scoped precisely. Avoid treating political instability as a score proxy.

dimensions.draft_judgement: The speeches document communication about war, the budget shock and coalition rupture. Scholz’s accusations against Lindner are attributed claims, not established facts. Their tone alone is insufficient to assess composure or proportionate crisis decision-making; contemporaneous advice, alternatives and the counterpart’s original account remain needed.
dimensions.uncertainties: The accusations are Scholz’s claims, not proved misconduct by Lindner. Whether the communication was proportionate requires context and the other side’s original account; effects and decision quality remain incomplete.

dimensions.draft_judgement: The record includes attributed acceptance of responsibility for the party result, a direct statement accepting the Court’s authority and a courteous handover. External analysis notes no apology in the budget speech; that observation does not establish absence of humility. The coalition accusations remain unverified claims and require context before they can qualify a personal humility judgement.
dimensions.uncertainties: Do not treat electoral defeat as a leadership score. Different views of responsibility and the original German wording require editorial judgement; absence of an apology in one speech is not proof of absence of humility.
